My name is known here in Tabora, and this small plot near my home I use for something different from my main fields. The rains here come once, from November to April, so I must prepare well and plant when the ground is soft. I do not have much money for chemical fertilizer on this small piece — maybe I put a little on part of it if my cooperative gives me some, but mostly I rely on what manure I can gather from the goats and what the land gives. I use my own seeds saved from last year because the improved ones at the shop in town cost too much, and for this plot me and my wife and older children will do most of the work ourselves with the hand hoe.
